tldr: AI startups captured 47% of all disclosed VC funding in November 2026, with $49.9B across 513 deals. The concentration is unprecedented and reshapes the funding landscape for every other startup category.
context:
The 47% share is a November figure compiled from disclosed rounds. The real total is likely higher, since many rounds go undisclosed. For comparison, AI's share of VC funding was roughly 30% a year ago.

The concentration is driven by mega-rounds in AI infrastructure and applications: Sierra ($1.75B), Hone Health ($228M for AI-powered longevity), Epochal ($100M for temporal web data), and dozens of $10M–$100M rounds in agent tools, security, and developer infrastructure.

In Europe, total VC hit a projected $81B for 2026, up 62% year over year, with Germany at $13.4B. But even in Europe, deal volume at the early stage is falling even as total dollars rise — fewer companies are getting funded, but the ones that do raise more.

The pattern: capital is bifurcating. AI companies with traction get mega-rounds. Everyone else competes for the remaining 53%.

whyPM:
When half the money goes to one category, it distorts everything: talent, pricing, partnerships. AI-funded competitors can outspend you on engineering, offer below-cost pricing to win customers, and attract talent with higher salaries and equity.

The flip side: if you're building an AI product, the money is there — but so is the competition. With 513 deals in one month, differentiation is harder than ever. Generic 'AI for X' pitches don't work when investors have hundreds of options.

For non-AI startups, the fundraising math is brutal: 53% of VC dollars, divided among many more companies. The strategic response is either to become AI-native or to compete in spaces where AI isn't the primary differentiator.
bull: AI's VC share peaks and stabilises as the best companies consolidate. Early-stage non-AI startups benefit from less competition and more focused investors. The $49.9B creates a generation of well-funded AI companies that become reliable enterprise vendors.
bear: Half the $49.9B is wasted on companies that can't differentiate. A correction wipes out the weakest, dragging down the whole AI brand. Non-AI startups starved of capital shut down, reducing ecosystem diversity.
